tierB-000129.notes: The rule form, the 0.9/0.9 TV with no QuantifierPhrase companion, Theme for 'use', the surface-form Manner filler 'wrongly' and the distributive split into two defeat events all follow the instruction set; only the premise's Skolem terms are off. gaps: a BOUNDED temporal gap ('more than a decade ago') — `BeforeBy` carries only an exact magnitude and there is no at-least/at-most gap form, while the TimeAtLeast/TimeAtMost route needs a TODAY that is not supplied, so the quantity is unrepresentable

issues: Asserts an air witness at strength 1.0 even though the only mention of air is inside the counterfactual antecedent 'there were no air', which supposes its absence — nothing in the text licenses a positive existential for it.

The consequent clause ('people could not live for even ten minutes') and the relation between the two clauses are entirely unrepresented — no live event, no negation, no duration, and no conditional or counterfactual wrapper.

negated-existential antecedent ('if there were no air') — a rule premise cannot yet mean 'X is not the case' (registered limitation), and the existential section covers only positive 'there is a X'
scalar 'even' on a bare duration under negation ('not live for even ten minutes') — `(Even <filler> <event>)` expects a constituent filler, with no slot for a measure or duration focus
tierB-001229.notes: A single atom was emitted and it asserts the opposite of what the antecedent supposes. The registered gaps explain why the conditional itself is hard to encode, but they do not license asserting the air witness.

tierB-001369.notes: The subject NP is handled correctly (definite → typed witness, and a merely descriptive adjective stays its own Member atom rather than fusing into a compound). `(Member sk_cat_1 poor)` is what the instruction set as written produces, though it records the wrong sense of 'poor'.

issues: The coordinated object 'Twilight and her friends' was distributed inside the complement (two stop and two recover events) but not in the matrix clause, leaving one invite event carrying two Theme atoms — the distributive shape replicates the whole predication, and the licensed collective shape is one event with multiple Agent atoms.

'stop the elements of harmony' takes Patient although its object is neither created/destroyed/physically changed nor an occurrence or informational artifact, so the unclear-case default of Theme applies (same for statement 14).

tierC-000044.notes: Names, the possessed-plural group witness plus `Possession` for 'her friends', the tenseless control complement, `PartOf` for 'the elements of harmony', and the purpose-infinitive `To` atoms all follow the instruction set. gaps: locating a group whose members are event-denoting nouns (earthquakes): the instruction set splits LocatedIn (entity) vs Location (event) by the event/entity line, but does not say which head a group witness over eventualities takes

an existential-there frequency claim restricted to a place ("there are a lot of Ns in P") has two candidate routes -- the existential group + CardinalityPhrase of *Cardinality*, and the kind-level ConditionalProperty route given for "Ns are common in P" -- and the instruction set does not say which applies
tierB-000364.notes: "a lot of" is on the vague-quantity list and here counts things, so CardinalityPhrase rather than a strength setting is correct, and the group takes no status atom (unmarked/generic present).

gaps: "one of the most ADJ Ns" -- a non-unique / top-tier superlative: Most encodes a unique maximum only, so the three coordinated superlative adjectives ("most systematic, subtle, and significant") have no licensed carrier and are dropped entirely

an argument PP on a PREDICATE NOMINAL in a copular kind clause ("X is a vehicle for V-ing"): the copular collapses to (Inheritance X vehicle), leaving no noun symbol for the prescribed (For <noun-symbol> <argument>) form to attach to
tierB-000436.notes: The instruction set says the For-argument's eventuality is "asserted nowhere", yet the spread event's class and role atoms sit at top level at (STV 1.0 0.99); they carry no tense, which matches the occurrence-neutral convention used for non-finite complements, so the requirement is ambiguous rather than plainly violated. Fusing racist_ideology with both a genus and an exposed adjectival modifier is licensed (racist is predicable of the ideology).

issues: the restrictive relative clause "in which one always cheats" restricts the predicate nominal "game", but the parse detaches it into a free-standing generic whose oblique points at love, so nothing records what kind of game love is said to be.

the impersonal generic pronoun "one" ("one always cheats") -- the pronoun rules cover only referential he/she/it/they with or without an antecedent, not the generic-human "one"

gaps: universal pronouns "everything" / "everyone" -- the quantifier machinery covers "every N" / "all the Ns" with an overt kind noun, but never says what range a bare universal pronoun takes (here the parse supplies (Member $y thing)) nor what surface word its QuantifierPhrase companion should record ("every" is recorded, the surface word is "everything")

a mode-of-perception PP ("see ... in black and white"): it answers "how", which the oblique rule routes to the named role Manner, but Manner is glossed as adverb-only, leaving the preposition-named In vs Manner choice undecided

issues: "also" sits in front of the whole coordinated predicate, so the ellipsis carries it into the second conjunct too, but the (Also ...) tag is emitted only for the first appear event.

gaps: life-stage temporal adjuncts ("later in life", "in his youth") -- the Time section covers calendar/clock terms, deictic constants, day-parts, frequency and interval forms, but nothing anchored to a participant's lifetime
tierC-000049.notes: The antecedent-less "he" is correctly a person-classed witness with its class atom, both compounds decompose correctly (noun modifier music left unexposed, adjectival modifier comedic exposed), and (Before sk_appear_1 sk_appear_2) is a licensed record of "later".

gaps: an intensifier modifying a spatial preposition ("right behind") — the only defined mechanism is the CamelCase join of a multi-word preposition, and "right" is a degree adverb rather than part of the preposition, so the intensifier has no carrier of its own

an institutional bare-noun locative frame ("in class") on a bare position clause — the clause mints no event, so there is no Location slot, and LocatedIn is defined as containment in a place rather than in an activity or institution
tierB-000375.notes: The bare position clause correctly mints no event for "sat" and wraps both position atoms in Past, with the non-containment preposition kept entity-attached, exactly as "Where a THING is" prescribes. gaps: a content noun's clausal complement ("the reputation of being an ambulance chaser") — the noun-complement rule says to reify a clausal argument while asserting it nowhere, and the sealing pattern is enumerated only for propositional attitudes, embedded questions, imperatives and counterfactuals, so nesting a proposition as a term argument of an entity-attached oblique has no explicit licence
tierB-000492.notes: Holder/Theme on the have-event, the definite subject's typing kept at top level, the surface preposition Of, and the non-assertion of the reputation's content are all right. issues: The result of "turn ... into sugars" is carried only by (Result (sk_turn $x) (sk_sugar $x)); the state-result shape also requires the reified result to carry an Experiencer naming what became it plus the flat copular atom, and neither is emitted.

a many-to-one material transformation with coordinated inputs ("turn A, B and C into D") — the change-of-kind/state-result shape assumes a single bearer that is identical to the result state's Experiencer, and nothing licenses saying that several inputs jointly become one product
tierB-001897.notes: The rule scaffolding is right: Skolem-function events per binding with no free variables, 0.9/0.9 for a bare empirical generic with no QuantifierPhrase, Theme for "use", subject control on the purpose event, main event first in (To ...), and the carbon_dioxide genus with the noun modifier unexposed. a bare quantificational pronoun ("nobody") — the quantifier machinery covers "no N" / "none of the Ns" determiners but never states the implicit domain kind such a pronoun ranges over
a deictic locative ("in there") — deictic TIMES are speech-anchored constants, but deictic places are never addressed
a verb + adjectival-complement fixed expression ("make sure") — no rule says whether it fuses into one surface symbol, decomposes as a resultative (make + sure), or is a control/attitude verb

tierB-000354.notes: Definite subject as a typed witness, transitive inanimate subject as Agent, unchanged object as Theme, Past, and the named time `midnight` as a bare Time symbol all follow the instruction set as written.

a degree adverb on a relational predicate ("only distantly related") — Manner is for event adverbs and Degree takes a single bearer, so a scalar adverb over a two-place relation has no slot

a three-word compound kind ("annual breeding cycle") — the decompose-once rule is stated for two-word modifier_noun pairs, so which of the two modifiers rides in the symbol and which gets a genus is left to judgment

gaps: a bare quantificational pronoun ("everything") — the quantifier machinery covers "every N" / "all the Ns" determiners but never states the implicit domain kind such a pronoun ranges over, nor what fills the kind slot of its QuantifierPhrase companion

a proverbial / gnomic generic with an indefinite singular subject ("A woman thinks …") — the determiner rule forces a witness for a verbal predicate, which records the sentence as being about one particular woman rather than as the generalization it states

tierB-000420.notes: Bare-plural generic to a distributing rule at 0.9/0.9, "like that" as the explicitly licensed (Like ...) oblique on the rule variable, no QuantifierPhrase companion, and the unrepresentable adverbial omitted — all as instructed. bare comparative with no stated standard ("warmer", no "than" phrase) — More and MoreBy both require two compared arguments
absolute "with NP + predicate" adjunct expressing a circumstance/condition ("with friends nearby") — the "with"-phrase split given is only CoAgent vs Instrument

'other' as a contrastive / anaphoric modifier ('other goats' = goats distinct from the buck already introduced)

an individual-level 'when'-clause supplying the circumstance under which a gradable state holds - ConditionalProperty is kind-level (kind + property + condition symbol), not an individual bearer with a clausal condition
a bare locative adverb with no prepositional object ('there were other goats around')

tierB-000027.notes: The phrasal verb kept whole as `fish_out` with no genus, the `fishing_trawler` compound genus with the noun modifier left unexposed, the definite-plural group witness, and the distribution rule for the descriptive modifier "local" all follow the instruction set.

issues: The concessive force is lost: no atom relates the searching to the denied finding, and (Even sk_town_1 sk_search_1) instead reads "even the town searched", while in the sentence the particle scopes over the whole with-clause set against the main clause.
"the WHOLE town" is reduced to a bare (Member sk_town_1 town) — the totality quantification is dropped entirely.

(Ongoing sk_search_1) matches none of the four explicit Ongoing markers the instruction set allows (progressive auxiliary, continuative perfect, inceptive complement, perception-verb participle) — the -ing here is an absolute participle.
gaps: "even with NP V-ing" — a preposition + absolute participial adjunct expressing concession; the connective section covers subordinating conjunctions (although / even though / despite) and the focus section covers a particle sitting on a constituent, but neither covers this augmented-absolute construction or says whether the adjunct's event carries tense of its own
"the whole N" as a totality modifier on a singular collective noun — the quantifier lexicon runs all/every/most/a lot of/many/few/no, and "whole" maps to none of them
tierB-000348.notes: The "no one" negative universal as a strength-0.0 distribution rule over (Member $x person) with its companion, Theme for the found person, and the projected Name/property atoms for little Fadil outside the denial all follow the instruction set.

tierB-000970.notes: "The Durga puja" is split into (Name durga "Durga") + (Member durga puja) exactly as the rule for a lowercase common noun beside a capitalized name prescribes, and the agentless passive simple present correctly carries no status atom. The coordinated locative is replicated once per conjunct under the distributive default, with the performed puja shared across both events.

issues: The subject "This" gets no witness and no class atom and nothing is predicated of it, so the sentence's entire copular claim is absent — the instruction set makes the witness plus its class atom mandatory for an antecedent-less pronoun and bars an untyped referent.
"one of the greatest mysteries" is reduced to a lone mystery witness: the definite superset of mysteries, the membership link from the subject, and the superlative "greatest" are all unencoded.
"in ALL of science" drops the universal — the atom records only the bare domain.
gaps: copular "X is one of the ADJ-est Ns" — membership in a superlative-restricted definite set: Most/Ordinal encode a unique single-entity superlative, and the partitive machinery is written for a quantified subject or object, not for a copular predicate naming the set the subject belongs to
emphatic universal over a mass/domain noun ("all of science") — the quantifier-to-strength route and the partitive route both need a count range or a predication to attach to
tierB-001144.notes: The one head used, In, is the licensed framing/domain oblique. What is emitted is not false, it is a small fragment of the sentence.

issues: "often" is encoded only by lowering that single atom's strength to 0.8, with no QuantifierPhrase companion, so the frequency word itself is unrecorded and is indistinguishable from a hedge on the time — the instruction set requires the companion whenever the word is actually there.
The hedge "AROUND Midsummer" is dropped: the Time atom records the bare named time as though it were the exact stated time.
gaps: a frequency adverb on a bare EXISTENTIAL ("there are often many parties") — the companion form is (QuantifierPhrase <kind> <verb-lemma> "<word>") and "there are" supplies no verb lemma, and nothing says which atom of an existential carries the frequency strength
approximation ("around / about") on a NAMED, non-numeric time — ParticleFromNormal is defined only for a numeric clock/calendar value, so the hedge on "around Midsummer" has no carrier
tierB-001571.notes: The group witness plus CardinalityPhrase "many" for the counted existential and the Name atom for Midsummer follow the instruction set; attaching Time to a group of event-denoting nouns extends the event-noun route to group level.

tierB-000431.notes: Copular individual predication, compound-kind genus on the fused symbol, and the agent-nominalization capability plus incorporated-object kind-relation all fire exactly where the instruction set licenses them (fused-from-surface symbol and copular predicate). The noun modifier 'demon' is correctly left unexposed and all decomposition atoms carry the definitional 1.0/0.99.

gaps: a relational of-phrase whose possessor is itself a PLURAL ('the members of the student associationS') — the Possessive/genitive NP rules attach one possessed symbol to one possessor, and there is no nominal-side dependent-witness machinery (Skolem functions exist only inside rules), so the per-association membership collapses to a single members-group PartOf a single associations-group
tierB-001066.notes: Definite plurals correctly take group witnesses rather than Inheritance; the passive by-phrase takes Agent, 'elect' takes Theme (choose-class, object unchanged), the present-tense habitual correctly carries no status atom, and the distributive predicate gets both the group event and the per-member rule at 1.0/0.9. 'on campus' correctly keeps the surface preposition entity-attached rather than folding into LocatedIn, with the article-less NP staying a constant.

issues: 'Such a thing' is an indefinite in a copular predication, which the Existential section routes to the generic kind (Inheritance), so minting the witness sk_thing_1 asserts one specific existing thing where the sentence makes a sort-level claim.
The explicit 'no' of 'of no account' is absorbed into the property symbol of_no_account and the atom is asserted at strength 1.0, so the denial the sentence actually makes is recorded nowhere.
gaps: predicative PP complement of the copula ('X is of no account') — the Two-kinds-of-clause split only covers 'is a/an N' and 'is ADJ', and the PP here is neither locative (Where a THING is) nor an argument PP of a noun/adjective (Complements of nouns and adjectives)
the anaphoric-kind determiner 'such a' — a thing of the contextually salient sort; nothing in the instruction set gives 'such' a carrier, so it is silently dropped

an explicit negation lexicalized inside a multi-word predicate ('no account') — a fused idiom symbol has no polarity slot, and the strength-0.0 route needs a positive counterpart atom to negate, which the surface never supplies
tierB-001290.notes: Both atoms are mechanically well-formed and the head (Member) is licensed; the defect is that the sentence's negative force and its 'such'-anaphora both vanish. The idiom-as-one-surface-symbol treatment is defensible per Compound concepts, but that section never contemplates a negative word inside the fused symbol.

gaps: a restrictive RELATIVE CLAUSE narrowing the subject kind of a copular kind-level generic ('spider bites THAT CAUSE FEVER are rare') — the instruction set puts a relative clause in the premises of an event rule, but 'rare' is a non-distributing KindProperty that must not distribute, and ConditionalProperty's condition slot is licensed only for an adjective/state, a measure/environment, or a locative/domain restriction, never for a clause

a contrastive discourse adverb set off by commas (', though,') joining two KIND-LEVEL, non-eventive claims — Inter-clause connectives requires two reified eventualities as endpoints and neither generic supplies one, and the defeasible-exception escape does not apply (scorpion_sting is not a sub-kind of spider_bite), so the contrast has no carrier and is dropped
tierB-001585.notes: Both compound kinds take their genus with the noun modifier correctly unexposed, both verb_object compounds decompose per Compound concepts, the modal 'can' over a kind correctly routes to the reified (can <action>) property at 0.9/0.9 rather than an event Can, and the restriction is correctly not stripped into a bare KindProperty. The ConditionalProperty encoding of the relative clause is the least-bad available shape, but the condition filler cause_fever is an action compound rather than a state, which is the gap above.

gaps: negation scoping over a DEGREE-modified adjective ('is not SO big') — Negation (copular) specifies the strength-0.0 (And ...) bundle for a noun-plus-modifier predicate ('not a legal dwelling'), and says nothing about whether a Degree atom joins that bundle or stays outside it, so whether the sentence denies being-big-to-that-degree or being-big outright is left undetermined by the instruction set
tierB-001660.notes: The definite NP mints a typed witness, 'in Prague' correctly takes the entity-attached LocatedIn (containment preposition, no eventuality), and Prague gets its Name with no kind atom invented since the text states none. 'so' is not in the listed intensifier lexicon but the rule to record the surface adverb lemmatized covers it, and the positive property is correctly withheld from top level under the denial.

gaps: frequency adverb ('regularly') on an imperative: the frequency-adverb strength bands and their QuantifierPhrase companion are defined only for a generic/habitual clause (the companion needs kind + verb-lemma arguments), Every/TimesPer require a stated period or rate, and a Directive's STV carries directive force rather than frequency, so nothing can carry 'regularly'
tierB-000641.notes: Imperative sealing, the coordinated-VP split into two Directives, the definite-plural group witness, and top-level typing of the projected definite referents all follow the instruction set. One structural hazard worth recording: (PartOf sk_exterior_1 sk_group_1) reuses PartOf's member-of-group sense, so any later per-member distribution rule ranging over (PartOf $x sk_group_1) would bind the exterior as though it were a cabinet.

issues: No (Symmetric Like) tag beside the relation, although 'are like' is exactly the stative mutual-by-meaning predicate the instruction set names ('is similar to', 'resembles'), so the reverse direction cannot be derived.
The explicit adversative connective 'but' is recorded nowhere - neither a surface-connective atom nor the defeasible-exception pattern - so the stated contrast between the two halves is lost.
gaps: adversative 'but' joining a clause to an elliptical predicative PP ('but without the shell'): the connective rule requires two reified eventualities as endpoints, and neither a preposition-headed kind relation nor a bare copular kind claim supplies one

privative 'without NP' as a predicate (absence / lacking): no defined encoding, and no route to a strength-0 claim either, since 'without' is not one of the explicit not/n't/no/never negators that the instruction set says are required to set strength 0.0
entity-attached preposition-named obliques are defined for entities and events; using them between two bare KINDS - (Like slug snail), (Without slug shell) - is not addressed
tierB-001301.notes: Like and Without are both licensed under the open surface-preposition licence ('like ...' is named explicitly in the never-coin-a-head rule), and the 0.9/0.9 truth values match the bare relational-generic band. Nothing is asserted beyond the words - in particular the shell is not attributed to snails.

tierB-001873.notes: Matches the eventive-boundary form for 'stopped V-ing' - a stop event plus the activity, both positive Past, the activity as Theme and the subject as Agent, which is the exact shape the instruction set's own cessation query template assumes. 'Old' is correctly left unfused as incidental description, and the -ly manner adverb keeps its surface form on the stopping event.

gaps: past-tense capability modal ('could be separated'): the status table gives (Can e) for 'can / able to' but no way to mark its past tense, and the 'a bare modal is the event's only status atom, add no tense beside it' instruction is stated only for the epistemic Might/Probably/Must

a descriptive or evaluative adjective on a bare mass kind used as a role filler ('true philosophy', 'popular wisdom'): the non-fusing branch of the adjective+noun test (distribute over members, or predicate copularly of a witness) has no target for a bare kind constant, so fusing is forced even where the modifier reads as description rather than a classifying subtype
tierC-000062.notes: Expletive 'it' dropped, the agentless-passive attitude reified with no Experiencer, the complement sealed with no predication of P at top level, and the definite 'this method' correctly projected - the impersonal-reported-attitude routing is followed exactly. The compound decomposition atoms carry the definitional 1.0/0.99 and the by-phrase is read as a means rather than an agent, which is right for a non-agentive 'by'.

issues: The degree adverb 'dangerously' in 'dangerously lax' is dropped with no Degree atom, so the intensity the sentence actually states is lost.
gaps: a degree adverb on a kind-level property that has been routed into ConditionalProperty: Degree's first slot takes an entity bearer (all its examples are individuals) and ConditionalProperty's property slot holds a bare property symbol, so there is no defined place to hang 'dangerously'
tierC-000157.notes: Both locative restrictions correctly go into the ConditionalProperty condition slot - the proper noun kept as its constant with its Name atom, 'the army' as a typed witness - with no bare Inheritance or KindProperty stripped of the restriction, and the two 'and'-coordinated clauses are parsed independently with no connective atom. The past copular wraps each kind-level atom as the surface tense requires.

issues: "should not" (a weak deontic recommendation) is encoded as an absolute prohibition — (Permitted e) at strength 0.0, confidence 0.99 — dropping the weakening the instruction set assigns to "should" (strength 0.7 on the positive), so the atom claims tempering is flatly impermissible.
gaps: negated weak deontic ("should not V" / "ought not to V"): the instruction set maps "should/ought" to (Obligated e) at strength 0.7 and maps prohibitions to (Permitted e) at strength 0.0, but enumerates the prohibition cues as "must not / may not / shall not / forbidden to" only, and never says how the two combine for a weak negative
tierB-000164.notes: Demonstrative "this steel" correctly typed as a projected definite witness outside the strength-0 bundle, and the agentless passive correctly gives the steel Patient (tempering is a treatment that changes it) with no Agent atom.

issues: The quantifier "few" is mis-slotted as a property symbol in ConditionalProperty's property slot, where the instruction set instead maps "few" to strength 0.1 plus a QuantifierPhrase companion; the atom as written asserts at strength 0.9 that career possibilities have the property `few`, which the seeded cond_prop rule would then hand to each individual possibility.
The exceptive "Aside from being a professor" is dropped entirely — no atom mentions professor, so the parse states the "few" claim without the excluded case the sentence carves out.
gaps: bare-existential quantity claim "there are few N": it has no subject-predicate pair for the Quantity-to-strength dial to sit on, and bare "few" (unlike "a few / several / a handful / dozens") is not in the CardinalityPhrase vague-quantity lexicon, so no licensed carrier exists for it

exceptive "aside from X" scoping over a quantified domain — the instruction set lists "aside from" only as a defeasible-exception cue introducing a SUB-KIND that lacks or reverses a generic property, not as an exclusion from an existential/quantified claim
speaker-oriented evaluative sentence adverb ("unfortunately") — Manner covers only event-manner adverbs; there is no licensed encoding for an evaluative comment adverb
tierB-000223.notes: The ConditionalProperty shape itself is licensed for the locative restriction "at the university" (the "berths are scarce at the marina" pattern), and the career_possibility compound genus with the noun modifier left unexposed follows the compound-kind rule correctly.

issues: "life in an urban slum" loses its restriction: the of-argument is recorded as bare `life`, and no atom links the slum to life (or to anything), so the parse asserts the movie is a depiction of life in general.
sk_slum_1 is typed but left dangling — it fills no role and stands in no relation, so the urban-slum witness contributes nothing to the parse.
gaps: a locative/framing PP restricting a bare mass or abstract noun used as a nominalization's of-argument ("depiction of life in an urban slum"): LocatedIn is barred from kind/entity-less arguments ("a kind is not a positioned thing") and there is no event for a Location oblique, so the instruction set names no carrier for the restriction
tierB-000347.notes: Splitting "harrowing depiction" into two Member atoms is right (incidental description, no fusion), and routing the nominalization's of-phrase to the surface-preposition oblique rather than Possession follows the instruction set; the "urban slum" fusion plus both genus atoms is borderline but internally consistent (urban is predicable of the slum, so its genus is required once fused).

gaps: copular-linking appearance verbs with an NP complement ("looks/sounds/feels/tastes like a paradise"): the instruction set routes *seem / appear* to the epistemic Might/Probably status and routes perception verbs with EVENTIVE complements to perception reports, but never says how "look like NP" is encoded — reifying a `look` event with the Like oblique is an extrapolation

an indefinite NP serving as the STANDARD of a likeness comparison ("like a paradise"): the existential rule mints a witness plus its class atom, which asserts that such a thing exists, although "X looks like a Y" makes no existential commitment to any Y
tierB-001135.notes: `Like` is explicitly licensed as the surface-preposition oblique, Experiencer is the right subject role for a stative intransitive, and "now" correctly stays a bare deictic constant with no calendar atoms (no TODAY supplied) and no status atom for the bare simple present.

gaps: concessive / contrastive "while" (= "whereas"): the instruction set lists "while" among the TEMPORAL connectives that take no connective atom and map to During, and never addresses its concessive sense, so the contrast between the two clauses has no licensed carrier here

a cause/concession/contrast connective joining two KIND-LEVEL clauses: the connective-atom form needs two reified eventualities as endpoints, but both clauses here are kind-level property claims (ConditionalProperty / partitive Inheritance) that reify no event witnesses
tierC-000040.notes: The partitive is textbook — definite superset, subset with SubsetOf plus ProportionOf most, and the property on the subset by Inheritance rather than Member; "in Canada" correctly goes in the ConditionalProperty condition slot as a bare proper-noun constant, and "related to prostitution" is correctly read as a reduced relative with the prepositional verb's object in the To oblique.

issues: The intensifier "quite" is dropped entirely — no Degree atom or any other record of the degree modifier on "uncommon".
gaps: degree intensifier ("quite") on a kind-level property carried by ConditionalProperty — Degree takes an entity bearer alongside an asserted positive property, but a ConditionalProperty deliberately does not assert the bare property, so there is no licensed slot for the level

a predicate NOUN under a locative restriction ("X is a(n) ADJ N in/at Y") — ConditionalProperty's property slot is documented for adjectival/state properties and reified deontic/capability terms, not for a predicate noun such as `sight`
tierB-000592.notes: Routing the locative-restricted, non-distributing rarity property to ConditionalProperty matches the "voles are common in the fens" pattern, and the indefinite copular subject correctly reads as the kind `man`. Splitting "an uncommon sight" follows the descriptive adjective+noun split rule, but it leaves an assertion that a man in the kitchen is a `sight` and predicates rarity of `man` rather than of the spectacle.

gaps: intensional / non-veridical object of *require* (likewise need, want, seek): the indefinite-argument rule mints an existential witness, so the parse asserts that a group of large repairs exists, whereas the sentence only says they are required — the instruction set offers no way to record an unasserted object
tierB-001436.notes: Roles follow the instruction set as written (a stative transitive subject stays Agent; requiring does not change its object, so Theme; bare simple present takes no status atom), and the descriptive modifier "large" distributes over the group's members with the prescribed 1.0/0.9 rule TV. The bare-plural object could alternatively have taken the bare class symbol `repair`, but that has nowhere to attach "large".

gaps: a PLURAL collective noun with a member-kind of-phrase ("large herds of cows") — the instruction set covers only the singular "a flock of birds" (Member + GroupOf) and gives no form for a group whose members are themselves groups, nor for placing a GroupOf atom inside a distribution rule's conclusion
tierB-001467.notes: Demonstrative plural to a group witness, "had" to Holder/Theme with Past, and "large" distributed to each herd (not to the cows) all follow the instruction set. The possession predicate gets no per-member distribution rule over the Tuareg group — defensible as a collective reading, though the plural/distributive rule would otherwise call for one since "have" is not a collective predicate.

gaps: terminological naming predication ("X are referred to as Y", "is called / known as Y") — the instruction set provides Name only for proper-noun string labels, so the term equivalence between the two kinds (predictive_function / pedotransfer_function) has no licensed encoding and survives only as an (As <event> <kind>) oblique on the refer event
"as" introducing a predicative complement — it is treated as a preposition-named oblique, which is the closest licence, but the instruction set never addresses a predicative (non-oblique) "as"-phrase
tierC-000206.notes: The agentless passive with the prepositional verb's object in the To oblique matches the "referred to the memo" rule; the demonstrative plural takes a group witness, both compounds carry their genus with the adjectival modifier `predictive` exposed and the noun modifier `pedotransfer` correctly not, and the non-spatial framing PP takes the In oblique with an ordinary witness for its indefinite NP. Simple present correctly gets no status atom, and "non-spatial" is a positive property at strength 1.0 rather than a negation.
